title: Prime-power Zolotarev (units): sign(x ↦ u·x on (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ) = legendreSym p (u mod p)
description: Performs the heart of the prime-power computation that the parent (the full squarefree-odd Frobenius/Zolotarev lemma sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n)) explicitly left as its #1 follow-up: 'handle prime-power factors pᵉ — the CRT does not split them and the sign on ℤ/pᵉ is a genuinely new computation.' For an odd prime p, exponent n ≥ 1 and a unit u : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ, the sign of the left-multiplication-by-u permutation of the unit group (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ equals the Legendre symbol mod p of the reduction of u. For a prime modulus the units form the multiplicative group of a field and Zolotarev's lemma is the field quadratic character; for a prime POWER, ℤ/pⁿ is no longer a field, yet (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ is still cyclic (ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow, for p odd), so the left-regular-representation argument still applies — but the value is now read off via the reduction homomorphism ρ : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ → (ℤ/p)ˣ rather than a field quadratic character. The proof: x ↦ u·x is left translation Equiv.mulLeft u in the finite group G = (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ; both sign ∘ mulLeftHom and legendreSym p ∘ ρ are homomorphisms G → {±1}, so as G is cyclic with generator g it suffices to check both equal -1 at g — a generator gives a single |G|-cycle with |G| = pⁿ⁻¹(p-1) even, and ρ g generates (ℤ/p)ˣ (ρ surjective) hence is a non-residue mod p. Writing u = gᵏ, both sides equal (-1)ᵏ.

overview.text: The squarefree induction of the parent stops at the squarefree case because the Chinese Remainder Theorem only separates COPRIME factors — it cannot peel a repeated prime out of pᵉ. The sign of multiplication on ℤ/pᵉ is therefore a genuinely new computation, and this entry supplies its harder half: the sign on the units (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ. The single observation that unlocks it is that (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ remains cyclic for odd p even though ℤ/pⁿ is not a field, so the same left-regular-representation / single-cycle-at-a-generator argument used for the prime base case carries over verbatim — the only adjustment is that the Legendre value is now obtained through the reduction map ρ : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ → (ℤ/p)ˣ (a generator reduces to a generator, hence to a non-residue) instead of a field quadratic character.
overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev (1872) identified the Legendre symbol (a/p) with the sign of x ↦ ax on (ℤ/p)ˣ. Frobenius (1914) generalized this to composite moduli and the Jacobi symbol. The lineage of gallery entries built this up in layers: the great-grandparent (oq-01-oq-03) formalized the CRT decomposition of the multiplication permutation on the whole ring ℤ/n; the grandparent (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01) proved the prime base case sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/p) = legendreSym p a; the parent (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01) performed the factorization induction over the prime factors to reach Mathlib's jacobiSym for all SQUAREFREE odd n, and explicitly left handling prime-power factors pᵉ (e ≥ 2) as its #1 follow-up, since the CRT cannot split them and the sign on ℤ/pᵉ is a different computation. This entry performs the heart of that new computation at the level of the unit group.
overview.problemStatement: Open Question (the listed next step #1 of elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01): handle prime-power factors pᵉ — the CRT does not split them and the sign on ℤ/pᵉ is a genuinely new computation; reaching it gives sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for every odd n. This entry computes the sign of the multiplication-by-u permutation on the units (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ — the genuinely new piece — leaving the assembly with the non-unit part p·ℤ/pⁿ to a follow-up.
overview.proofStrategy: Work in the finite group G = (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ. Part 0 (generic, any finite group): left translation is a monoid hom mulLeftHom : G →* Perm G (the left regular representation); translation by a non-identity element has no fixed point (mul_right_cancel) and a generator's translation is therefore a single full-support cycle; its sign is -(-1)^|G|, which is -1 when |G| is even. Part I: |(ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ| = pⁿ⁻¹(p-1) (ZMod.card_units_eq_totient + Nat.totient_prime_pow) is even because p-1 is. Part II: instantiate at G = (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ, cyclic by ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow (p odd). Take a generator g; the reduction ρ = ZMod.unitsMap (p ∣ pⁿ) is surjective (ZMod.unitsMap_surjective), so ρ g generates (ℤ/p)ˣ and is a non-residue (reusing the parent's generator_not_isSquare), giving quadraticChar(ρ g) = -1; the single-cycle argument gives sign(mulLeft g) = -1. Writing u = gᵏ, sign(mulLeft u) = (sign mulLeft g)ᵏ = (-1)ᵏ and quadraticChar(ρ u) = quadraticChar(ρ g)ᵏ = (-1)ᵏ, so they agree. legendreSym_unit_eq converts the field quadratic character of the reduced unit back into the Legendre symbol.
keyInsights: ℤ/pⁿ is not a field for n ≥ 2, so the prime base case's field quadratic character is unavailable — but (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ is still CYCLIC for odd p (ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow), and cyclicity is all the left-regular-representation sign argument actually needs.

x ↦ u·x on the units is left translation Equiv.mulLeft u in the group (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ; left translation by a generator of a finite cyclic group is a single |G|-cycle, whose sign is -1 exactly when |G| is even — and |(ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ| = pⁿ⁻¹(p-1) is even for odd p.

The Legendre value is recovered through the reduction homomorphism ρ : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ → (ℤ/p)ˣ: ρ is surjective (ZMod.unitsMap_surjective), so it sends a generator to a generator of (ℤ/p)ˣ, which is a non-residue mod p — this reuses the parent's generator_not_isSquare unchanged.

Both sign ∘ (left translation) and quadraticChar ∘ ρ are homomorphisms (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ → {±1}, so on a cyclic group they coincide as soon as they agree on a generator; writing u = gᵏ collapses the whole statement to (-1)ᵏ = (-1)ᵏ.
The fixed-point-free / single-cycle lemmas (Part 0) are stated for an arbitrary finite group, isolating the purely group-theoretic content of Zolotarev's lemma from the number theory.
prerequisites: The parent's prime base-case helpers (ZolotarevBaseCase.generator_not_isSquare and legendreSym_unit_eq)
(ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ is cyclic for odd p (ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow) and the reduction map is surjective (ZMod.unitsMap_surjective)
Cardinality of the unit group (ZMod.card_units_eq_totient, Nat.totient_prime_pow)
Sign of a single cycle (Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.sign) and the left regular representation (Equiv.mulLeft as a monoid hom)
Field quadratic character and the Legendre symbol (quadraticChar_neg_one_iff_not_isSquare, legendreSym)

sections.title: The left regular representation of a finite group (generic)
sections.content: mulLeftHom : G →* Perm G packages left translation as a monoid hom. mulLeft_no_fixed: translation by a ≠ 1 has no fixed point (mul_right_cancel). mulLeft_generator_isCycle / mulLeft_support_eq_univ: a generator's translation is a single full-support cycle. sign_mulLeft_generator: its sign is -1 when |G| is even. sign_mulLeft_pow: sign of translation is multiplicative under powers. These hold for any finite group and isolate the group-theoretic core.

sections.title: The prime-power unit group has even order
sections.content: card_units_prime_pow_even: |(ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ| = pⁿ⁻¹(p-1) via ZMod.card_units_eq_totient and Nat.totient_prime_pow, which is even because p-1 is even for an odd prime p.

sections.title: The units-level prime-power Zolotarev lemma
sections.content: sign_mulLeft_eq_quadraticChar and sign_mulLeft_eq_legendre: for an odd prime p and n ≥ 1, the sign of left multiplication by u on (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ equals the quadratic character (resp. Legendre symbol mod p) of the reduction ρ u. Proof: instantiate the generic machinery on the cyclic group (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ; both sides are -1 at a generator g (single even cycle; ρ g a non-residue), and u = gᵏ makes both (-1)ᵏ.

meta.author: Zolotarev (1872), Frobenius (1914)
meta.assumptions: None. The file has 0 axiom declarations, 0 sorries, no native_decide, and no assumption-carrying structures. Both headline theorems were checked with #print axioms and depend only on propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (the standard foundational axioms, which do not count as assumptions). Honest scope: this computes the sign of multiplication on the UNITS (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ — the genuinely new piece the parent flagged. Assembling it with the action on the non-unit part p·(ℤ/pⁿ) ≅ ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ to obtain the whole-ring statement sign(ringMulPerm u on ℤ/pⁿ) = J(u | pⁿ), and thence every odd n, is left to a follow-up. No new axioms are introduced.

conclusion.summary: Proves, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the units-level prime-power Frobenius/Zolotarev lemma: for an odd prime p, n ≥ 1 and a unit u : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ, the sign of the left-multiplication-by-u permutation of (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ equals the Legendre symbol mod p of the reduction of u. This is the heart of the prime-power computation the parent's squarefree induction could not reach, because the Chinese Remainder Theorem does not split repeated prime factors. The argument reuses the prime base case's generator-is-a-non-residue lemma but replaces the field quadratic character with the reduction homomorphism (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ → (ℤ/p)ˣ, the only adjustment needed once one observes (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ is cyclic.
conclusion.implications: Supplies the genuinely new computation flagged by the squarefree parent: the sign of multiplication on a prime-power modulus, at the level of the unit group. Combined with the action on the non-unit part p·(ℤ/pⁿ), this would extend sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) from squarefree odd n to ALL odd n. The generic Part 0 also isolates the purely group-theoretic core of Zolotarev's lemma (sign of left translation in a finite group), reusable for any cyclic group of even order.
openQuestions: Assemble the whole-ring prime-power statement: decompose ringMulPerm u on ℤ/pⁿ over the invariant units / non-units partition (Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypeCongr), identify the units part with this entry's sign(mulLeft u) and the non-unit part p·(ℤ/pⁿ) with ringMulPerm of the reduced unit on ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ (the map y ↦ p·ỹ intertwines the two actions), and induct on n to obtain sign(ringMulPerm u on ℤ/pⁿ) = (legendreSym p u)ⁿ = J(u | pⁿ).

Combine the per-prime-power result with the great-grandparent's CRT multiplicativity (sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd) to obtain sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for EVERY odd n, completing the Frobenius generalization.
Specialize the resulting general-odd statement to recover quadratic reciprocity itself (Zolotarev's original application).
